item.title: Leitrim issued status yellow ice and snow weather warning
item.description: Leitrim has been issued a status yellow ice and snow weather warning. This warning comes into effect from 2 o'clock tomorrow morning and will also affect Sligo and Donegal. It will end at 2 o'clock in the afternoon. Advertisement Met Éireann has warned of poor visibility and difficult traffic conditions. item.title: €1.5m allocated to Carrick on Shannon bypass project
item.description: €1.5 million has been allocated to the Carrick-on-Shannon bypass project by Transport Infrastructure Ireland. The project involves a 6-kilometre road around the town, from the Dublin Road to the Boyle Road. The entire Carrick bypass will cost up to €500 million and aims to address big traffic problems in the town. item.title: Three Critical Mental Health Roles Withdrawn in West Roscommon
item.description: Three critical mental health positions in west Roscommon have been withdrawn. The HSE says they've been decommissioned from the E-Mental Health Hub in Castlerea. The facility opened in 2020 at the former Rosalie Home. Advertisement Sinn Féin's Claire Kerrane says three positions have now been decommissioned whilst there are also three vacant positions in the CAMHS Connect Service. item.title: 628 Patients Waiting for Hospital Beds Nationwide This Morning
item.description: 628 patients are waiting for beds in the country's hospitals this morning. Locally Sligo University Hospital continue to be busy with 37 admitted patients on trolleys this morning. Elsewhere Midland Regional Hospital Mullingar have just 6 patients waiting for a bed while Portiuncula Hospital have no patients on trolleys. Advertisement Nationally 398 are waiting in Emergency Departments while 230 are waiting elsewhere in the hospital.

item.title: Funding boost for Longford-Mullingar road upgrade - as €6m announced
item.description: A total of €6 million has been allocated to the upgrade of the N4 between Longford and Mullingar. The money has been assigned today by Transport Infrastructure Ireland. It is expected the upgrade will cost between €500 million and €1 billion and will now move through the statutory and appraisal stages, with construction commencing by 2030. item.title: €90m for completion of Ballagh to Scramogue N5 upgrade
item.description: A total of the €90 million has been allocated for the completion of the upgrade of the N5, between Ballaghaderreen and Scramogue. The money has been assigned by Transport Infrastructure Ireland today. The cathaoirleach of Roscommon County Council, Liam Callaghan, says the project is well advanced: Advertisement A total of €300,000 has also been allocated to the upgrade of the Clashaganny to Tulsk road. Councillor Callaghan says it's very welcome: Advertisement

item.title: Major jobs boost for Longford - as cyber-security company announces 80 new roles
item.description: A total of 80 jobs have been announced for Longford. They're being created by cyber-security company ZeroRisk, which is setting up a new facility in the Axis Centre, just outside Longford town. The company serves some of the biggest financial institutions in the world. Advertisement Taoiseach Micheál Martin says the 80 jobs are a huge boost to Longford and the surrounding region. item.title: Blow to Aldi's Boyle plans - as appeal lodged over planning go-ahead
item.description: Roscommon County Council's decision to grant planning permission for a new Aldi store in Boyle has been appealed to An Coimisiún Pleanála. The German supermarket chain applied for planning permission to build the supermarket and refurbish five houses on Patrick Street. Roscommon County Council granted planning permission, subject to 36 conditions, last month.
